questions.prompt: At each step, what does a language model produce?
options: A corrected copy of the prompt
questions.explanation: A model predicts one likely next token, adds it to the text, and then predicts again.

questions.prompt: Why must a program surround a language model to get work done?
options: The model runs too slowly on its own
The model cannot read a prompt by itself
The model has no goal and only continues text
The model forgets the token it last wrote
questions.explanation: A model only continues the text it receives. It has no goal or memory, so a program must give it a task and a way to act.

questions.prompt: The prompt is "The capital of France is". The model returns " Paris". What text does the model read at the next step?
options: The capital of France is Paris
Paris is the capital of France
questions.explanation: Each new token joins the text, and the longer text goes back to the model for the next prediction.
